slides.heading: WHIP PAN TRANSITION
slides.subheading: Match direction and speed—or the cut feels accidental.

slides.heading: WHY IT MATTERS
bullets: A whip pan transition connects scenes with blur and energy.
Shoot whip out and whip in at the same speed and direction on set.
Cut at peak blur—neither frame should be sharp at the edit point.

slides.heading: CUT AT PEAK BLUR
slides.caption: In post, directional blur 2–4 frames each side can fake the move.

slides.heading: WORKFLOW
steps: Shoot whip out and whip in on set.
Cut at peak blur on both sides.
Add directional blur in post if needed.
Sync to whoosh SFX or a music hit.

slides.heading: PRO TIP
slides.text: Plan the exit and entry framing before the first whip.

slides.heading: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.text: Mixing whip directions in the same sequence.
